intent: Split three more linux_configuration scripts, and harden the verifier after a split silently corrupted a file.
scope: meta/scripts/verify_shell_split.sh (lib parse check moved ahead of the entry lint)
changes: Nine libs across three scripts, each needing a second carve after the first pass.

enforce_vbox_hosts.sh was reverted because the split landed INSIDE a heredoc: the resulting lib had an unterminated here-document and bash -n rejected it outright. This is the first split in the whole effort to produce a file that does not parse, and it is the most dangerous failure mode yet - shellcheck reported it only as SC1094 'parsing of sourced file failed' on the caller, which reads like a linting nicety rather than a broken file.
The verifier now runs bash -n over every lib BEFORE linting the entry, and names the offending lib with a hint about heredocs. Proven in both directions on a deliberately corrupted copy.
Fixed another unguarded cd, this one before `git clone ... .` - a failed cd would have cloned an AUR repo into the caller's working directory.

ALLOW_WEB and ALLOW_DNS are declared in the entry, set by the arg parser in one lib and read by the ruleset builder in another; exported, which is what SC2034 asks for and makes the three-way contract explicit.

verification.evidence: All three now report 'libs sourced, functions defined'. Four real failures on the way: chained libs in all three, the unguarded cd, the exported flags, and the vbox heredoc corruption.

verification.command: append an unterminated heredoc to a lib, re-run the verifier, restore
verification.evidence: Reports the here-document parse failure and exits non-zero; passes again once restored. Tested in both directions, because a check that never fires is worse than none.

verification.command: git checkout HEAD -- enforce_vbox_hosts.sh, rm its lib dir, bash -n and shellcheck -x
verification.evidence: Restored to 443 lines, parses and lints clean.
Clean, including shellcheck over each lib in isolation.

risks: None of the three was run: they install CUDA runtimes and AUR packages, start user services, and rewrite sshd and nftables configuration.

The heredoc failure means the function-boundary heuristic the splitter uses is not safe on files with heredocs at top level. bash -n now catches it, but only after the fact - the splitter itself still has no awareness of heredocs.
enforce_vbox_hosts.sh stays at 443 lines and needs a seam chosen by hand, outside any heredoc.
rollback: git revert the commit; the three scripts return to their previous sizes, the nine libs disappear, and the verifier loses its parse check.
After rollback, re-run bash -n and shellcheck on the restored scripts.
